name: SambaCry: CVE-2017-7494
short_description: Exploit the SambaCry vulnerability for remote code execution via Samba shares.
description: SambaCry (CVE-2017-7494) is a remote code execution vulnerability in Samba versions 3.5.0 to 4.6.4. It allows uploading a shared library to a writable share, then executing it. Similar to EternalBlue but for Linux Samba. NOTE: The Metasploit module may show 'no session created' due to a known framework bug - the payload DOES execute (check server logs with 'docker logs samba').

steps.title: Verify SMB is running
steps.explanation: Scan for SMB/Samba ports. Port 445 is SMB over TCP.

steps.title: Enumerate Samba shares
steps.explanation: List available shares without authentication (-N = no password). Look for writable shares.
steps.expected: Sharename list with 'data' or similar writable share

steps.title: Show options
steps.explanation: Review required settings. Need RHOSTS and SMB_SHARE_NAME.

steps.title: Set target host
steps.explanation: Set the vulnerable Samba server IP.

steps.title: Set writable share
steps.explanation: The share where we'll upload our payload.

steps.title: Set SMB username
steps.explanation: This share requires authentication. Username: sambacry

steps.title: Set SMB password
steps.explanation: Password: nosambanocry (weak credentials found via enumeration)

steps.title: Run the exploit
steps.explanation: Upload and execute the payload. Due to a known Metasploit bug, you may see 'no session created' but the payload DOES execute on the server.
steps.expected: Backdoor service spawned OR 'no session created' (known MSF bug - payload still executes)

steps.title: Verify payload execution (in another terminal)
steps.explanation: Since the MSF session handler has a bug, verify RCE by checking server logs. Look for 'Module loaded' which proves your payload executed.
steps.expected: Module '/data/<random>.so' loaded - proves remote code execution!

steps.title: One-command pwn (after you learn it)
steps.explanation: Exit the shell (type 'exit' twice) and try this. Now that you understand the attack, this script runs it automatically.

success_criteria: Logs show 'Module loaded' - proving remote code execution. Due to a known Metasploit bug, you may not get an interactive session, but the payload DOES execute with root privileges on the target.
next_steps: Research: Why doesn't the MSF session work? Check GitHub issue #13977
Try a custom .so payload that creates a reverse shell manually
Learn about SMB1 vs SMB2/3 compatibility issues
